chapter_note: Heavily lacunose chapter preserving a substrate teaching about the progressive differentiation of the dark pentad: five elements → five worlds → five trees/fruits → five creations of flesh → ten parts (male/female) → twelve parts (adding fire and lust) mapped to the twelve zodiac signs. The enumeration structure ('first part'... 'fourth part'... 'fifth time') is the skeleton of the teaching, though gaps make reconstruction difficult. Editorial fatigue is textbook: substrate dominates ¶2-7, then ¶8-9 apply the twelve-part mapping to 'the holy church' and 'the twelve sects,' and ¶10 closes with devotional formula. The substrate teaching is the oldest layer and is dominant in this chapter despite the lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: the two essences [...] Did Death arise and stand firm [...] up? Or else did it turn itself from [...] its armour [...] in its [...] but it finished [...] the two [...].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame opening: 'Once again, the enlightener is sitting in the midst of his disciples, explaining to them about the great and secret matters of God [...]' and 'His disciples say to him [...]:' — formulaic frame attribution wrapping a substantive cosmological question about the two essences and the arising of Death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The question is substantive: it asks about the two essences (dualistic cosmological categories) and how Death arose. This defines the teaching topic. Frame formula is standard Kephalaia dialogue_frame vocabulary ('Once again, the enlightener is sitting'). The honorific 'great and secret matters of God' is frame language, but 'the two essences' names the cosmological topic and is preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.48⟩ [...] it moved it and [...] they that are in the [...] of the earth of Darkness [...] first part.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extremely fragmentary but contains substrate markers: 'earth of Darkness' (cosmic geography) and 'first part' (beginning of an enumeration sequence). No editorial or institutional vocabulary. The enumeration marker places this as the beginning of a systematic degree-teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, after a long time, as there was not [...], it gushed and streamed up [...] the five elements of Death that gushed [...] which are smoke, fire, wind, water and darkness [...] the second time [...] they were sculpted [...] those in which Death was established [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate: the five elements of Death enumerated (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) — the standard dark pentad. Process vocabulary ('gushed and streamed up', 'sculpted', 'established') describes cosmic generation. High substrate score (25.0). 'The second time' continues the enumeration sequence. Death functions as a personified cosmic agent throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth part is the evil fruits [...] in the five trees that are in the five worlds of the land of Darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration marker ('The fourth part') continuing the degree-teaching. Maps fruits → five trees → five worlds → land of Darkness. All correspondences stay within the cosmic system. High substrate score (26.09). The five trees mapped to five worlds is a classic correspondential structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth time it spread itself out to its creatures that exist in the five worlds; the ones that were formed and generated from the five fruits of Death. They are the five worlds of flesh, the five creations of Darkness in which Death has been established. It spread itself out to ten parts, five male parts and five female [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the enumeration ('The fifth time'). The key cosmological move: the five creations of flesh divide into male and female, yielding ten parts. This doubling is the structural core of the chapter. All mappings cosmos→cosmos: five worlds → five fruits → five creations → ten parts (5 male + 5 female). High substrate score (21.31).

paragraphs.core_text: Now, like the land of Darkness, in that its spirit and its [...] they nourished the five elements [...]; this is also [how] the ten parts that are in male and female, the fire and lust of the flesh [...] them, as they yoke them with one another [...] they were established against the First Man. This is [...] of the Darkness, it was condemned for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summarizes the cosmic process: ten parts (male/female) energized by fire and lust, yoked together, established against the First Man. All within the cosmic system — no contemporary institutions referenced. 'Now, like' is comparative syntax, not an editorial bridge connective here since it introduces a cosmic analogy (land of Darkness nourishing elements → ten parts yoked). 'Condemned for ever' describes the cosmic fate of Darkness within the dualistic system. The First Man is a cosmic figure, not a contemporary reference.

paragraphs.core_text: Alongside the mystery of these twelve parts that came about in the Darkness [...] against the First Man. The twelve [...] the twelve spirits of error that came about from the twelve signs of the zodiac [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps twelve parts → twelve zodiac signs → twelve spirits. Despite 'spirits of error' firing editorial_bridge vocabulary (13.51), the actual mapping stays cosmos→cosmos: the spirits COME FROM the zodiac signs, which is a cosmological-correspondential relationship. The editorial application of these spirits to contemporary institutions only begins in ¶8. The twelve-fold structure (ten parts + fire and lust = twelve) mapped to the zodiac is the culmination of the substrate's degree-teaching. Classified as substrate because both sides of the mapping remain within the cosmic architecture.

Clear editorial pivot: 'the second living man, who dwells in the holy church' applies the First Man pattern to the Manichaean community. 'Holy church' is institutional vocabulary (13.89 institutional score). The comparison ('the way that they pursued [...] at the beginning of the First Man') explicitly bridges the cosmic substrate to contemporary community experience. One side of the mapping now reaches outside the cosmic system into the editor's ecclesial present. This is exactly where the editorial fatigue pattern predicts later-layer material.

Continues the editorial application: 'the light that dwells in the church' and 'the twelve sects' map the cosmic twelve-part structure onto the editor's contemporary religious landscape. Both editorial_bridge (20.0) and institutional (20.0) scores fire strongly. 'The twelve sects' is a specific identification of contemporary religious groups — the mapping has crossed from BEING to POINTING AT. Very fragmentary but clearly editorial.

Devotional closure fragment: 'his holy father for ever and ever' — standard beatitude/doxological closing formula. Exhortation score (37.5) is the highest of any score in this paragraph. Positioned at chapter end, consistent with editorial fatigue pattern. Too fragmentary to determine more, but the formula is characteristic of the devotional closure layer.
